tiles.name: SC filter
tiles.subtitle: MAX7410
tiles.result: a 5th-order Butterworth low-pass at fCLK / 100 (up to 15 kHz from a 1.5 MHz clock on IO3); the clock's images near fCLK
notes: MAX7410: a switched-capacitor ladder whose corner is the clock divided by 100, clocked from IO3 through an SN74LV1T34.
IN and OUT sit at COM (2.5 V), so both are AC-coupled.  Sweep the clock and watch the corner follow; alias a tone.

tiles.name: SC integrator
tiles.subtitle: TMUX4053
tiles.result: an integrator whose input resistor is 1 / (f x 1 nF): 1 M at 1 kHz, 1 k at 1 MHz; OUT = -(1 / R C) x the integral of IN
notes: phi1 (IO4) connects the 1 nF's top plate to IN, phi2 (IO8) its bottom plate to the summing node: C x Vin per cycle at f,
a resistor of 1 / (f C).  Make the phases non-overlapping, or overlap them and watch IN leak through.  1 M sets the DC gain.

tiles.subtitle: TLC555
tiles.result: a square near 6.9 kHz on OUT (5 V divided to about 1 V); CV moves it: up as CV falls, down as it rises
notes: TLC555 astable: f = 1.44 / ((1 k + 2 x 10 k) x 10 nF), the capacitor between 1/3 and 2/3 of the supply.  CV pulls the
upper threshold through 2.2 k: a voltage-to-frequency converter.  Count OUT's cycles in the FPGA and you have an ADC.

tiles.name: cascode
tiles.result: gain about -6 into a high impedance (-8 at Q1's collector), half that into 50 ohm; common emitter (jumper on) about 2 MHz wide, the cascode (jumper parked) several times wider
notes: Q1's collector-base capacitance, multiplied by the gain (Miller), meets the 2.2 k at its base; the cascode holds Q1's
collector still, so only one Ccb counts.  The jumper on the header shorts the cascode out: compare the two sweeps.

tiles.name: delta-sigma
tiles.subtitle: second order
tiles.result: a one-bit stream on IO7 whose density follows IN (+-1.65 V full scale), its noise shaped at 40 dB per decade
notes: Clock IO1 at about 1 MHz and count IO7's ones.  The second integrator pushes the quantization noise up at 40 dB per
decade (AMOD-A's a6 is first order: 20 dB), so a sinc3 decimator gets more bits per clock.  INT1, INT2: high impedance.

tiles.name: comparator
tiles.subtitle: TLV3201
tiles.result: BIT on Pmod IO2 is high while IN is above DAC; a SAR search in gateware gives 12 bits in 12 steps of the DAC
notes: TLV3201 (40 ns, 1.2 mV hysteresis) on the 3.3 V rail.  Each input is averaged with the rail through a matched pair
of 0.1 % 10 k, so +-1 V lands at 1.15-2.15 V on both pins and the comparison is unchanged.  20 k input impedance:
drive it from a 50 ohm source, read the bit on IO2.  A successive-approximation ADC: the gateware sets the host's
DAC, reads the bit, halves the step; a tracking ADC: up when high, down when low; a slope ADC with a ramp on DAC.

tiles.name: regulators
tiles.subtitle: buck, LDO, load
tiles.result: BUCK~ shows the buck's 1.5 MHz ripple (a few mV, pulse-skipping below about 150 mA); LDO~ the same after the LDO, 40 dB smaller; LOAD sets 100 mA per volt
notes: TLV62568: 3.6 V from 100 k / 20 k; TRIM through 100 k into the feedback node moves it (0 V: 4.2 V, +1 V: 3.2 V, open: 3.6 V).
TPS7A2033: 3.3 V, about 92 dB of PSRR at 1 kHz and 40 dB at 1 MHz; below 3.5 V in it drops out (lower TRIM's voltage).
The load: an OPA810 servos 10 ohm to LOAD's voltage through an AO3400A (1 k and 1 nF slow its loop): a square on LOAD
is a load step.  Keep it under 100 mA for long (the shunt is 1/8 W), steps can be larger.  Both outputs are AC-coupled.

tiles.name: charge pump
tiles.subtitle: ICL7660A
tiles.result: about -5 V on the output, falling with load as 1 / (f C) + the switches: 2 k at 1 kHz, 80 ohm at 100 kHz (the pump at half IO6's clock)
notes: ICL7660A: switches charge the flying 1 uF across the supply and dump it, upside down, into the output's 1 uF.  IO6
clocks it through an SN74LV1T34 and 1 k; with 1 k of load, sweep the clock and read OUT: Rout = 1 / (f C) + 60 ohm.

tiles.name: differential pair
tiles.result: OUT = -1 k x (Ic1 - Ic2): +-1 V, tanh of (IN+ - IN-) / 2 VT, linear within about +-25 mV of balance
notes: A matched NPN pair (DMMT3904W: 2 mV of VBE, 2 % of hFE) on a 1 mA tail; a matched PNP pair as the mirror; an OPA810
holds the output node at 0 V and turns the difference current into volts.  Sweep IN+ with IN- at 0 V: the tanh, its
slope gm = Itail / (4 VT), about 10 mS here; a triangle in becomes a sine-like wave out when it is driven past balance.

tiles.name: rectifier
tiles.subtitle: precision
tiles.result: OUT = |IN| from DC to about 100 kHz; above that the first stage's slew across the diodes leaves a glitch at each zero crossing
notes: Stage 1: inverting with BAT54S in its feedback, so its node X follows -IN for positive IN and stays at 0 for negative.
Stage 2: OUT = -(IN + 2 X) = |IN|.  No dead zone from the diodes (the op amp's gain hides their drop) until the op amp
must slew through two diode drops at each zero crossing: watch the glitch grow with frequency.

tiles.name: track and hold
tiles.subtitle: LF398
tiles.result: OUT follows IN while IO5 is high and holds when it falls: 4 us to acquire, about 30 mV/s of droop, a few mV of hold step
notes: LF398 on +-5 V (its minimum supply: inputs within +-1.5 V).  1 nF C0G: acquisition about 4 us, droop about 30 mV/s.
Measure the acquisition time, the droop, the pedestal (the hold step) against IN, the feedthrough of a sine while
holding, and the aperture delay against the FPGA's edge on IO5.

tiles.name: power
tiles.subtitle: USB-C 5 V in: +5, -5, +3.3 out
tiles.result: +5 V from the USB-C (up to 1.5 A), -5 V at 40 mA, +3.3 V at 300 mA; the green LED says 5 V is in, the red one that -5 V is up
notes: USB-C power only: 5.1 k on each CC asks any source for 5 V.  A 2 A PTC, a 5 V TVS (clamps at 9.2 V) and 20 uF.
The LM2664 charge pump makes -5 V for the op-amp tiles (40 mA: four tiles at 10 mA); it is not switched per tile, an op
amp with its +5 V removed draws nothing.  The TPS7A2033 makes 3.3 V for the comparator and the lines that meet the FPGA.
The socket along the top carries +5, ground, -5, ground, +3.3: the bench's rails for a breadboard experiment.

back_text: AMOD-C: power and data conversion, switched
capacitors and transistors.  USB-C 5 V on c1.
